messages.subject: nimbleFunction doesn't work after compilation
parts:
Good Afternoon
I am trying to split a dataset in nimble using nimble list. it's working fine when i call the function directly but returns an error
"Error in if (cSizeExprs$args[[1]]$nDim != 0) nonScalarWhereNeeded <- TRUE :
  argument is of length zero"
when i try to compile it. 
Any help would be highly appreciated.


y=rlnorm(200,2,0.5)
NimListDef <- nimbleList(y1 = double(1), y2 = double(1))

Y <- nimbleFunction(run=function(y=double(1),u=double(0)){
 
  NimListDef$y1=array()
  n1=1
  NimListDef$y2=array()
  n2=1
  for(i in 1:length(y))
  {
    if(y[i] < u)
    {
        NimListDef$y1[n1]=y[i]
        n1=n1+1
    }
    else  
    {
      NimListDef$y2[n2]=y[i]
      n2=n2+1
    }
  }
  return(NimListDef)
  returnType(NimListDef())
})
Y(y,10)
works fine
assign('Y', Y, .GlobalEnv)
Y1 <- compileNimble(Y)
Error in if (cSizeExprs$args[[1]]$nDim != 0) nonScalarWhereNeeded <- TRUE :
  argument is of length zero

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: nimbleFunction doesn't work after compilation
parts:
Hi Arnab,

Thanks for the question.

The main problem is that nimbleList returns a nimbleList definition, i.e. generator or class definition.  It looks like you then want a list object, which is created by NimListDef$new().

Other issues are that the vectors y1 and y2 (in a NimListDef object or not) will not automatically extend themselves by assignment past the current value. And for compilation nimble is statically typed, so you should use numeric instead of array to create a vector.

Below is code that does what I think you want and works.  And further below is a more compact version.  The NIMBLE User Manual at r-nimble.org has sections on nimbleLists and object types.

Y <- nimbleFunction(run=function(y=double(1),u=double(0)){

  obj <- NimListDef$new()
  y1=numeric(length = length(y))
  n1=1
  y2=numeric(length = length(y))

n2=1
  for(i in 1:length(y))
  {
    if(y[i] < u)
    {

y2[n2]=y[i]
      n2=n2+1
    }
  }
  if(n1 > 1) obj$y1 <- y1[1:(n1-1)]
  if(n2 > 1) obj$y2 <- y2[1:(n2-1)]
  return(obj)
  returnType(NimListDef())
})

Y(y, 10)
cY <- compileNimble(Y)
cY(y, 10)


More compact version:
Y <- nimbleFunction(run=function(y=double(1),u=double(0)){
  obj <- NimListDef$new()
  y_lt_u <- y < u
  obj$y1 <- y[ y_lt_u ]
  obj$y2 <- y[ !y_lt_u ]
  return(obj)
  returnType(NimListDef())
})

Y(y, 10)
cY <- compileNimble(Y)
cY(y, 10)

HTH
Perry
